Course 04

Personality without labels

Traits, differences and assessment.

Lesson 4. Does personality change?

1 · Lesson

Personality is fairly stable but not immutable. Longitudinal studies, which follow the same people for years, show a pattern called the maturity principle: on average, conscientiousness and agreeableness increase and neuroticism decreases with age, especially between 20 and 40.

Experiences also matter: a new job, a relationship, becoming a parent, a health problem. And some studies suggest that psychotherapy can produce change, especially in emotional stability.

Traits have a heritable part (twin studies place it roughly around half of the variation between people), but heritable does not mean fixed: heredity sets tendencies that interact with the environment throughout life.

2 · Example

Someone who at 20 was messy and absent-minded may, at 35, be the one who organises family holidays. They did not "change personality" overnight: new responsibilities and roles gradually reinforced certain behaviours, which over time became part of who they are.

3 · Activity

Compare yourself with the person you were ten years ago. In which trait have you changed most? What experiences do you think played a part? Write down a change you would like to make and which concrete behaviour would represent it.
